ai.description: Chandel’s toad reaches 4–5 cm. It is brown with dark dorsal blotches and a pale mid-dorsal stripe. Key features include a blunt snout, prominent parotoid glands, and heavily tubercular skin.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Duttaphrynus manipurensis* is best distinguished by the presence of a distinct, continuous, and prominent cranial ridge that extends from the snout to the parotoid gland.
ai.habitat: Duttaphrynus manipurensis inhabits the subtropical evergreen forests of Manipur, India, typically found at elevations between 800 and 1,200 meters.
ai.behavior: Duttaphrynus manipurensis is primarily nocturnal, emerging after dusk to forage for small invertebrates among the leaf litter of its forest habitat.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Duttaphrynus manipurensis* breeds during the monsoon season (June–August), depositing eggs in long, gelatinous strings within shallow, stagnant water bodies.
ai.distributionRemarks: Duttaphrynus manipurensis is endemic to the state of Manipur in Northeast India, where it inhabits high-elevation areas within the Indo-Burma biodiversity hotspot.
ai.callDescription: The advertisement call of *Duttaphrynus manipurensis* consists of a series of short, pulsed, high-pitched notes, typically heard from vegetation near streams in hilly habitats.
